caseno:
Criminal Appeal No. 89 of 1986 with 
Criminal Misc. No. 24 of 1990.
lawyer:
MA Aziz, Advocate ----- For the Appellants.  
Md. Altaf Hossain, Advocate ----- For the State.
parties:
Kashem Molla & ors ----- Appellants 
Vs.
State ----- Respondent.
full_judgment:
Abdul Hasib J: This Appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 27.2.1986 passed in Sessions Case No. 67 of 1985 by Mr. Mohammad Aynul Hoque, Assistant Sessions Judge, Court No. III Khulna convicting the accused appellants under sections 395/397/412 of the Bangladesh Penal Code and sentencing each of them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 7(seven) years and also to pay a fine of Tk. 7000/- each in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a further period of 1 year and 3 months. 

 2. The prosecution case is that informant Habibur Rahman and 4 others are men from District Gopalganj. They went to Koyra PS in Khulna to purchase paddy. On 3.1.85 while they were sleeping at night in their বাছারী boat asking Momrej Kazi to keep watch, these 4 accused appellants along with others armed with gun, dagger, ballam and lathi came in a Dingi boat near the বাছারী boat of the informant party and struck the head of Momrej Kazi with an oar (বৈঠা). They looted the paddy, money and other materials amounting to Tk. 15,700/-. After dacoity the accused left. On hearing the hue and cry people from the nearby boats and places came and the informant Habibur Rahman narrated the occurrence to them. On 4.1.85 at about 11.30 AM the informant lodged the FIR with OC Koyra police station. 

 3. The police investigated into the case and submitted charge-sheet against these appellants and others under sections 395/397 & 412 of the Bangladesh Penal Code and they were placed before the Court for their trial. All the accused persons pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. At the trial the prosecution examined as many as 7 PWs and tendered two namely PW 5 & 6. Defence did not examine any. Their plea was one of innocence. 

 4. PW 1 Habibur Rahman who is the informant in this case deposed that on 3.1.1985 he along with Milu Kazi, Amrej Kazi, Karamot Ali Shaikh and Nasir Fakir went to Koyra PS and anchored their "বাছারী বোট" near the village Arjunpur. They went to sleep asking Momrej Kazi to keep guard. At about 11 PM 9/10 dacoits came to their boat, struck Momrej Kazi on the head with an oar (বৈঠা) and tied up all of them inside the boat. Thereafter they took the boat to village Chowkuni and started looting paddy, cash and other goods from inside the boat. The whole operation took about 2 to 3 hours. At the time of retreating one of the inmates caught hold of dacoit Mohammad Ali and another dacoit Salam fired a gun shot in the head of Keramat. Thereafter the dacoits fled away. At the time of commission of the offence he could recognise accused Sobhan and Kashem. Accused Salam and Mohammad Ali were guarding while other accused were looting. Accused Salam had a gun in his hand. Accused Salam and Mohammad Ali were recognised by other inamtes. At that time they started hue and cry and the other boatmen and people from nearby places came. He narrated the whole occurrence to them. On 4.1.85 at around 11.30 AM the Officer-in-Charge of Koyra Police Station came to their boat and he wrote the FIR which the informant signed. Thereafter the house of accused Sobhan was surrounded and paddy and some other looted articles were recovered from his house. In the cross-examination he stated that they used to go there every year to buy paddy and they know some of the dacoits. His evidence was taken by SP in Chalna. He further stated that he did not see any gun in the hand of accused Salam. He went to see injured Keramat 4/5 days after occurrence. There was no TI Parade. 

 9. PW 8 Golam Rahman was OC at the relevant time. He stated that at that time Joyjuddin was SI in that police station. He wrote the Ejahar in a white paper Ext. 2 and read it out to the informant and he signed it in his presence. Informant's signature is Ext. 1 and OC's signature is Ext. 2(2). He inspected the place of occurrence and prepared the sketch map Ext. 7 and his signature is Ext. 7(1). Index is Ext. 8 and his signature Ext. 8(1). He seized the boat which was given in Jimma and took the statements of the witnesses. He also wrote for the expert opinion about the gun and the opinion has been submitted. On finding a prima facie case he submitted charge-sheet. In his cross-examination he stated that except accused Sobhan and Kashem no witness told him about the recognition of any other accused. He also stated that Keramat did not tell him about the recognition of accused Salam and Mohammad Ali. Lutfor Rahman did not tell him that Salam fired the gun shot at Keramat or that Keramat caught hold of accused Mohammad Ali. He did not examine any doctor from Koyra. The gun that he seized from the house of accused Salam had a licence. The wife of Lutfor Rahman Shaikh, father of accused Salam, took out the gun from the house. He denied that the seizure list was false or that he prepared it at the instance of PW 7 Lutfor Rahman Sana and chairman Sahabuddin. He said that he did not know whether Lutfor Rahman Shaikh had any enmity with the Chairman or that the purpose of his seizing the gun was to take the gun out from the possession of Lutfor Rahman Shaikh. 

 12. Mr. MA Aziz, the learned Counsel for the accused appellants, submitted that the FIR story of the prosecution and the evidence given by the informant is not consistent. In his deposition the informant has improved the prosecution case by stating that he recognised accused Salam and accused Mohammad Ali. Whereas in the FIR he mentioned about the recognition of accused Kashem Molla and Sobhan Molla only. In his deposition he mentioned by name that accused Salam and Mohammad Ali were guarding the boat while other accused were looting. This fact was not mentioned in the FIR. The informant also mentioned that the FIR was given to the Officer-in-Charge in his boat in Koyra but in the deposition he stated that he sent people to Thana with a written Ejahar. Then the Officer-in-Charge came to Koyra and he handed over the ejahar to the officer-in-charge there. This ejahar was on a white paper which he signed. According to Mr. Aziz the deposition is an embellishment over the FIR and his evidence of recognition of accused Salam and Mohammad Ali cannot be believed. The prosecution witnesses stated that all the accused came without any mask and if they were known to the informant party they would not have come in that way. He further submitted that on the question of recognition the depositions of PWs were not uniform. Next submission of Mr. Aziz was that important seizure list witnesses like the Union Parishad Chairman and the Union Parishad member did not come to depose in this case. Lutfor Rahman Shaikh, father of accused Salam, had enmity with the chairman and the chairman was interested to get the gun out of the possession of Shaikh. Lutfor Rahman. This will be evident from the fact that the chairman was all along with the Officer-in-charge in the house of Lutfor Rahman Shaikh 4o seize the gun. 

 19. Coming to the question of sentence, we are of the opinion that in the facts and circumstances of the case and more so when conviction under section 397 is not sustainable as stated above, ends of justice will be sufficiently met if the sentence of appellants Kashem and Sobhan is reduced from 7 years to the period which they have already undergone in jail. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed so far as accused appellant Kashem Mollah and Sobhan Mollah are concerned with the modification that their conviction is altered from section 397 to 395 of the Penal Code and sentence reduced from 7 (seven) years to the period they have undergone in jail without any fine. The appeal of accused appellant Abdus Salam and Mohammad Ali is allowed, and the order of their conviction and sentence is set aside and they are acquitted of the charge brought against them. They shall be set at liberty if not wanted in connection with any other case. 

 The connected Criminal Miscellaneous case filed by Abdus Salam for bail is accordingly disposed of.
